item.title: GDB Debugging Workflow: Compiling, Setting Breakpoints, and Execution Flow
item.description:
“GDB Debugging Workflow: Compiling, Setting Breakpoints, and Execution Flow”

How does one effectively commence debugging with the GNU Debugger (GDB), encompassing necessary compilation steps, defining points of interest, and navigating program execution flow?

Debugging compiled programs often requires embedding symbolic information during the compilation phase, which GDB then utilizes to map machine instructions back to the source code. A robust debugging workflow involves several key steps: compiling, loading the binary, setting breakpoints, running the process, and inspecting state.
